source_user: Advanced cluster case cluster scheduling and recovery-37: Design a resilient cluster scheduler for distributed LLM training and inference. Variant 37 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: cover gang scheduling, GPU/NIC/topology-aware placement, fragmentation, preemption, checkpoint cadence, node drain, elastic restart, replica routing, SLOs, and resource accounting. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
For variant 37, define resilience as a measured scheduler-and-recovery property, not an assumed platform feature. Assumptions: jobs declare GPU type/count, CPU, memory, storage, NIC/RDMA, NUMA and GPU topology, DP/TP shape, priority, checkpoint format/interval, and inference SLOs; inventory, admission, placement, preemption, fencing, routing, and failure events are observable. Platform semantics and capacity are unknown until measured.

Hypothesis: topology-aware gang admission with fragmentation-aware packing, checkpoint-aware preemption, and bounded node-drain recovery will reduce wasted GPU-hours and p95 recovery time without degrading inference availability or latency versus the current policy. Keep workload mix, model, inventory, checkpoint policy, and routing policy fixed in matched baseline and canary windows.

Design: admit distributed jobs atomically only when GPU/NIC/NUMA constraints fit; expose queue reasons and fragmentation rather than partially starting a gang. Reserve topology-compatible capacity and account CPU, memory, storage, GPU-hours, and network capacity. Preempt only eligible work after a verified consistent checkpoint, recording lost work. For drain or failure, cordon and fence the node, verify checkpoint integrity, restart only when the elastic parallelism contract permits it, and route inference away from unhealthy or overloaded replicas. Use least privilege, audit every state transition, and provide a dry-run and rollback path; do not infer fencing or elastic guarantees without platform evidence.

Measure queue/admission time (s), placement failures, fragmentation (GPU-hours), GPU/NIC utilization (%), checkpoint interval/size (s/GB), preemption loss (GPU-hours), drain, restart, and recovery time (s), restart count, duplicate/lost work, request p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), error rate (%), availability (%), SLO violations, and resource-accounting error (%). Synchronize clocks, define sampling windows, report distributions and confidence intervals, and compare matched baseline/canary results stratified by job shape, topology, priority, load, and failure type. Confounders include changing workload mix, hidden throttling, topology drift, warm caches, checkpoint storage contention, clock skew, and correlated node failures.

Rollback if recovery p95 or SLO violations breach the predeclared budget, checkpoint validation fails, duplicate work appears, fencing is unverified, accounting error exceeds its threshold, or availability regresses; disable the policy, restore the prior admission/placement/routing rules, and preserve logs and checkpoints. Evidence required before claiming improvement: inventory/topology snapshots, policy version, workload and failure injection protocol, raw synchronized event traces, matched baseline and canary samples, checkpoint-integrity results, confidence intervals, and independent review.
risks: Platform-specific fencing, elastic restart, and topology semantics may differ from assumptions.
Synthetic scenario lacks measured workload and failure traces.
evidence_required: Topology and inventory snapshot
Matched baseline/canary traces with synchronized timestamps and units
Checkpoint integrity and recovery results
Independent domain review before operational claims
